structure: ZHU2010 is usable as partial marginal evidence, not as a representative target cohort or a source of dependence estimates. Its two cutoff counts and ferritin geometric mean constrain the model after explicit, unverified transport. Hb has a bounded truncated-normal marginal. Ferritin has a continuous two-piece log-scale marginal, allowing a broad low-ferritin tail without forcing the narrow spread implied by a single lognormal fitted only to the supplied geometric mean and cutoff probability. An assumed Gaussian copula supplies otherwise unidentified dependence. Each row is an independent virtual person; source evidence is not multiplied by the generated cohort size.

parameter_provenance.rationale: Reported count and denominator at the matching strict cutoff Hb <12 g/dL. Conversion from 120 g/L is division by 10.
Reported count and denominator at the matching strict raw ferritin cutoff <15 ug/L.
Uses the admitted ferritin units. No SD, SE or interval width is inferred.
Source estimates are transported unchanged as population-law parameters. This is not an identified estimate for the NHANES complete-measurement, phlebotomy-weighted domain.

parameter_provenance.parameter: Hb marginal shape, scale and support
parameter_provenance.rationale: A central adult Hb distribution with bounded positive support. These are modeling choices, not estimates from the omitted Hb location or ambiguous concentration intervals.
Population-level location calibration conditional on the assumed shape and support; implemented by deterministic bisection, not realized-sample recentering.
For low ferritin, log(F/15) is minus a half-normal with this scale. It allows substantial variation below the cutoff; the supplied evidence does not identify that variation.

For a standard half-normal, E|Z|=sqrt(2/pi). Thus E(log F)=log(15)+sqrt(2/pi)*[(1-p)*s_upper-p*s_lower]=log(17.4). This scale is conditional on the assumed two-piece family and transported constraints.

An illustrative modest positive association between iron stores and Hb. Neither its magnitude nor the Gaussian dependence family is identified by the supplied marginal evidence. This is not a raw Pearson correlation, residual correlation, adjusted association or multilevel coefficient.
Quantile probabilities are restricted to [1e-15,1-1e-15] to prevent floating-point infinities. This changes only extreme machine-level tails and is not sample-moment calibration.

requested_estimands.support_basis: Both marginal cutoff probabilities are evidence-anchored after assumed transport, but their joint allocation is not. In the ideal continuous model let J=Phi_2(Phi_inverse(258/1671),Phi_inverse(504/1671);0.35). The population crude odds ratio is J*(1-p_h-p_f+J)/[(p_h-J)*(p_f-J)]. Generated-table analysis must use the requested cells and return not estimable if any cell is zero.
key_unresolved_assumptions: Unchanged transport of both cutoff prevalences to the target domain.
Assumed latent correlation 0.35 and Gaussian-copula threshold dependence.
No source joint table or target weighting information identifies this crude odds ratio.

requested_estimands.support_basis: In the ideal continuous model the joint prevalence is J=Phi_2(Phi_inverse(258/1671),Phi_inverse(504/1671);0.35). This is an assumption-dependent model quantity, not a reported source joint prevalence. Without dependence assumptions, the transported marginal constraints permit J anywhere from 0 to 258/1671.
key_unresolved_assumptions: The source marginal probabilities apply to the target complete-measurement domain.
The chosen copula adequately represents lower-tail co-occurrence.
Unmodeled inflammation, menstrual loss, contraception and other anemia causes may alter the joint allocation.

requested_estimands.support_basis: No continuous rank coefficient is supplied. For the ideal continuous Gaussian-copula law, population Spearman correlation is (6/pi)*asin(0.35/2), because both marginal quantile maps are increasing. Thus its numerical value is imposed by the dependence assumption rather than learned from the source marginal summaries.
key_unresolved_assumptions: The Gaussian copula and latent correlation 0.35 represent the target's unadjusted rank dependence.
Raw ferritin affected by inflammation may have a different or nonmonotone relationship with Hb.
The continuous, unrounded measurement model omits assay rounding and resulting ties.

limitations: Source women were rural Chinese, parous, 2–4 years postpartum, using IUD contraception and subject to health exclusions. Target age, geography, parity, contraception, disease mix and selection differ; no transfer function is identified.

Positive phlebotomy weights and complete measurements define the target domain, but no target weights or selection model are supplied. Equal-weight generated rows represent that domain only under the stated transport assumptions.
Tables I and IV concern the same women and are not independent evidence. No joint statistics were supplied, and none were inferred from omitted fields.
The source Hb location and ambiguous concentration intervals were not used. The ferritin unit interpretation follows the admitted evidence rather than inconsistent printed units.

Dependence is deliberately nonzero but wholly assumed. Different admissible copulas or correlations can materially change all three requested analyses while preserving the supplied marginal summaries.

Ferritin has positive support and finite moments of every positive order because each log-side is half-normal. Its ideal upper tail is unbounded; there is no disease-specific high-ferritin component. The piecewise density can jump at 15 ug/L, an artificial feature not established biologically.
Hb is restricted to 5–18.5 g/dL. This excludes rare extreme measurements that could occur in the target; their frequency is unknown. Its assumed dispersion is not identified by the cutoff count.
There is no CRP restriction or inflammation adjustment. Inflammation-associated ferritin elevations and non-iron anemia are represented only implicitly by the joint distribution.
Finite generated samples fluctuate around the model law. They do not quantify evidence uncertainty, transport uncertainty or uncertainty about the assumed shapes and dependence.
checks_actually_performed: Analytically verified that the ferritin branch probabilities give P(F<15)=504/1671 and that the derived upper log scale gives E(log F)=log(17.4) in the ideal continuous law.
Analytically verified that the Hb location equation targets the transported strict-cutoff probability within the selected truncated-normal family.
Checked the mathematical construction for positive ferritin, bounded positive Hb, finite relevant moments, and a valid latent correlation.
Statically reviewed the generator for seed-controlled independent rows, ordered output columns, unique integer identifiers, and absence of sample-wide moment forcing.
No code execution, generated-data inspection or empirical moment checks were performed; no execution tools were available.
